fresh_leads.qualification_text: Frontend Software Engineer Intern - Summer 2027 San Mateo, California, United States Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions. About the role Skydio's mission is to make the world safer and more efficient through autonomous drones. Public safety, critical infrastructure, and enterprise customers rely on Remote Flight Deck (RFD), Skydio's browser-based piloting experience, to get eyes on the scene in seconds and coordinate a response. As a frontend intern on the RFD Platform team, you will help build that experience. RFD is the product the customer flies from, so the work starts in the interface and reaches into video, telemetry, and the services behind it when the feature calls for it. The RFD Platform team builds the browser platform every remote pilot uses: live video, telemetry, the map, and flight controls. As an intern, you will ship production features with engineers, designers, and product managers, and you will have room to follow a problem past the frontend when that is where it leads. HOW YOU'LL MAKE AN IMPACT - Design and implement pilot-facing features that help operators make faster, safer decisions while flying. - Leverage curiosity, technical skill, and a collaborative mindset to help make the world more productive, creative, and safe with autonomous drones. - Collaborate across functions (product managers, designers, engineers, and support) to deliver high-quality, impactful features to customers. PROJECT EXAMPLES - Build on the multi-cockpit view that allows pilots to open several drone pilots at once. - Ship a camera control like click-to-focus. Hold F, click a point in the live video, and lock focus and exposure on a moving target - Add a map layer like the flight-path breadcrumbs where pilots can turn on a live trail of where the drone has flown. - Render AR bounds around subject tracks from the vehicle, and allow users to interface to instruct the drone to follow a vehicle. WHAT MAKES YOU A GOOD FIT - Solid software engineering foundation and a commitment to writing clean, well-architected code. - Junior, senior, or MS-level student with meaningful project or internship experience developing modern web applications that connect to backend APIs and data systems. - Experience in modern web development (React, TypeScript, GraphQL, WebGL/Three.js). - Experience building and maintaining scalable APIs, services, and integrations for handling large datasets. - Bonus: familiarity with robotics software development concepts. What Makes You a Good Fit: - Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions. Compensation: The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Graduate students, and $70/hr for PhD students*. fresh_leads.qualification_text: Summer Research Program Intern 2027, AI and Geospatial Analysis for Natural Hazards (04-47) (Lexington, MA, US) Lexington, MA, US The Energy Systems Group at MIT Lincoln Laboratory develops technology solutions that enhance the resilience and efficiency of both civilian and defense infrastructure systems. This includes conducting strategic analyses to assess natural and adversarial threats to critical infrastructure sectors, identifying and developing technology solutions to mitigate these risks and enhance resilience, and developing hardware and real-time simulation testbeds. The Energy Systems Group seeks a summer intern to work within a multi-disciplinary team developing an AI-enabled portfolio analysis capability. Using agentic AI, the team will integrate DoW-funded R&D documentation with technical and geospatial data to identify trends and gaps, assess prior investments, and guide future research addressing natural-hazard risks. The candidate will help design and implement these AI-based analysis tools. Tasks may include: Developing agentic AI workflows for extracting, connecting, and analyzing information across technical documents Integrating GIS and natural hazard data to assess geographic coverage, needs, and portfolio gaps Developing and evaluating prototype analysis and visualization tools The software and analyses produced by the candidate will contribute to an enduring portfolio-analysis capability used to inform future research investments and operational priorities. Candidates who are pursuing a B.S., M.S., and/or Ph.D. in computer science, data science, engineering, applied mathematics, geographic information science, or a related technical discipline will be considered. Candidates must have strong problem-solving skills, work well independently and in teams, and possess effective written and oral communication skills. A successful candidate is required to have Python software development experience and demonstrated capability or interest in a subset of the following areas: Large language models, AI agents, RAG, or related AI/ML methods GIS, geospatial analysis, and spatial data processing Data engineering, visualization, and quantitative analysis Natural hazards, infrastructure resilience, or systems analysis Summer Research Program Overview The Summer Research Program offers students the chance to apply their academic knowledge to real-world national security challenges while working alongside leading scientists and engineers. As an SRP intern, you'll engage in hands-on research, receive dedicated mentorship, and take part in professional development opportunities including workshops, tech talks, and networking events—all while building connections within a vibrant community of peers. Internships are typically 10–12 weeks, with flexible start and end dates, typically May through early August. Housing support is available for eligible non-local interns, including access to discounted university housing in Boston and a one-time taxable relocation payment. Complimentary daily shuttle transportation is provided from Boston-based housing to and from the Lab.
